evals.name: clean-brief-single-spec
evals.prompt: Here's the brief for our candidate screening automation. Turn it into a spec we can build from.
evals.expected_output: One spec, no decomposition, no interruption. Should assign all four automation levels per step, state that no fallback is independent of the tracking system, and carry the brief's non-blocking OPENs forward without resolving them.
assertions: Produces ONE spec - does not decompose a single process
Does not interrupt with questions when no blocking OPEN exists
Names no tool, vendor, or platform
Assigns all four automation levels (collect/interpret/decide/act) per step
States explicitly that no fallback route is independent of the tracking system
Specifies that degradations are recorded, not only failures
Observation covers all three horizons: now, accumulated, trending
Carries the brief's non-blocking OPENs forward without silently resolving them
No rule is stated in more than one place
Spec length is proportionate to the process

evals.name: blocking-opens-must-be-resolved-first
evals.prompt: Can you plan out this invoice routing automation? Brief attached.
evals.expected_output: Stops before specifying and asks about the three blocking OPENs. When the authority matrix cannot be resolved, does not invent a mapping — separates what is buildable now from what is gated, and keeps the blocking item visible.
assertions: Asks about the blocking OPENs BEFORE writing the spec
Asks no more than 3 questions in a single round
Does NOT invent an approver mapping to fill the unresolvable blocking gap
Separates what can be built now from what is gated on the unresolved matrix
Names no tool, vendor, or platform
Specifies duplicate detection on more than invoice number, per the re-sent PDF finding
Names the touchless-percentage measure as fighting the duplicate rule, and states which wins
The unresolved blocking item remains visible in the delivered spec

evals.name: multi-process-should-decompose
evals.prompt: Here's our incident response brief - please turn it into a spec.
evals.expected_output: Decomposes into parent plus child specs on stated evidence. Children carry contract blocks, shared preconditions sit in the parent gate, failures are classified hard or soft, and no rule is repeated across artefacts.
assertions: Decomposes into a parent spec plus child specs
States the specific evidence for decomposing (triggers, owners, finished conditions)
Each child spec carries a contract block: guaranteed by parent / consumes / produces / escalates
Puts shared preconditions in the parent gate rather than repeating them per child
Classifies failures as hard (halts) or soft (continues with a flag)
Identifies the paging fallback chain as sharing a failure domain
Names no tool, vendor, or platform
Names the postmortem-completion-rate measure as fighting quality, and states priority
No rule is repeated across parent and children - each stated once where enforced
Child specs are substantially shorter than the parent, not photocopies of it
